hero.badge: Every photo verified before it is sent
hero.headingPart1: See a problem in your city?
hero.subtext: Potholes, floods, blocked drains, broken streetlights. Take a photo, drop the pin on the map, and City Care sends your report straight to the authority responsible for it.
hero.coverage: Built for Tanzanian cities, ward by ward.

how.title: From your phone to the right authority
how.subtitle: Four steps. No forms to collect, no queue at the council office.

snap.title: Snap and describe
snap.desc: Take up to five photos, choose the problem type, and drop the pin on the map so the exact spot is recorded.

verify.title: AI checks the photo
verify.desc: Before anything is saved, the image is compared against your description. A photo that does not match is rejected on the spot.

route.title: Routed to the right office
route.desc: Every problem type belongs to a registered authority. The verified report goes to the nearest one that handles it.

track.title: Track until resolved
track.desc: Follow your report as it moves from verified to assigned, in progress, and finally resolved.

problems.title: Thirteen kinds of problem, one place to report them
problems.subtitle: Pick the type that fits and City Care already knows which authority owns it.

why.title: Reports that authorities can actually act on
why.subtitle: A complaint on social media disappears. A verified, located, routed report does not.

verifiedPhotos.title: Verified photos only
verifiedPhotos.desc: Every image is checked against the description before the report is stored, so authorities stop drowning in noise and fake reports.

exactLocation.title: Exact location
exactLocation.desc: Pick the spot on the map and the report carries the coordinates, region, district and ward with it.

rightAuthority.title: The right authority
rightAuthority.desc: Roads, water, waste and streetlights all belong to different offices. Each report is routed to the one registered for that problem type.

staysInformed.title: Nobody is left guessing
staysInformed.desc: The assigned office is notified by email the moment a report lands, and you see every status change on your side.

cityInsight.title: Insight for the city
cityInsight.desc: Reports become statistics: which problems dominate, where they cluster, and how many residents are reporting them.

swahiliFirst.title: Swahili and English
swahiliFirst.desc: The whole platform works in both languages, because reporting a pothole should not require English.

faq.title: Everything residents ask us
faq.subtitle: Short answers to what comes up before the first report.

whatCanIReport.a: Potholes, flooding, blocked drains, broken streetlights, illegal dumping, damaged roads, sidewalks and bridges, traffic problems, water leaks, sewer problems and other public infrastructure faults.

whyPhoto.q: Why does a photo matter so much?
whyPhoto.a: The photo is the evidence. It is checked automatically against the problem type and your description, which is what lets an authority trust the report without sending someone to look first.

rejected.q: My report was rejected. What happened?
rejected.a: The photo did not match what you described, so it was not saved. You will see the reason and the relevance score. Take a clearer photo of the actual problem and submit again.

whoReceives.a: The authority registered for that problem type, and the nearest one when several cover it. They are notified by email as soon as the report is verified.

canIEdit.q: Can I edit a report after sending it?
canIEdit.a: Yes, while it is still submitted, verified or assigned. You can fix the description, change the type, adjust the location or replace photos. Once work has started it is locked.

tracking.q: How do I know anything is happening?
tracking.a: Each report carries a status: verified, assigned, in progress, then resolved. You see it change on your reports page.

anonymous.a: The authority sees the report, the photos and the location. Your account details are not published anywhere public.

cost.a: No. Reporting a problem in your city is free.

organisation.q: I work for an authority. How do we join?
organisation.a: Register through Partner with us. An administrator sets up your organisation and selects the problem types you are responsible for, and reports of those types start reaching you.

cta.heading: The pothole you pass every morning
cta.headingLine2: can be fixed. Start by reporting it.
cta.subtext: It takes half a minute: a photo, a sentence, and a pin on the map. City Care does the rest.

about.headingLine2: We make sure someone hears about them.
about.para1: Most urban problems are reported by nobody. Not because people do not care, but because there is no simple way to tell the right office, and no way to know whether the message arrived.
about.para2: City Care closes that gap. A verified photo, an exact location, and a named authority for every report, so a problem stops being everybody and nobody's business.
